verdicts.reason: A breaks the flavour grid into a jumbled text stack: names in reverse order, descriptors cut off from their flavours, and the yellow fine print sits above the descriptors. One giant can leaves two tiny orphan cans stranded bottom-left, and the CTA is pushed into the bottom-left corner next to the badge. B has the same jumbled text stack and orphan cans, and it also crams the CTA and badge against the top-left beside an off-centre logo, which leaves a large dead area at the bottom. A keeps the logo centred above the headline, so it is slightly less bad.

Both have the same broken structure. The CTA and ONLINE ONLY badge are jammed top-left above the product, the flavour names are listed in reverse with their descriptors split off, the fine print is promoted mid-stack, and two tiny cans float in the bottom-left over a dead lower third. A's headline runs almost to the canvas edges with almost no margin, and its top cluster hugs the left edge. B keeps slightly better side margins.

A dissolves the three-flavour grid into a reversed list with no grouping, inflates one can and shrinks the other two to tiny orphans, and buries a small CTA in the bottom-left corner. B keeps the original hierarchy, order and grouping: headline, three cans with their own names and descriptors, line of copy, centred CTA, fine print. Its only flaws are minor: the cans sit small in the wider canvas, and the can labels and footer text are tiny.

A keeps the original structure intact, with headline, three grouped cans and descriptors, centred CTA and fine print. It only needs polish: the cans could be larger for the wider canvas, and the label and footer text are very small. B puts the CTA and badge in a cramped top-left cluster, lists the flavours in reverse with their descriptors split off, shows one oversized can with two tiny orphan cans, and leaves the bottom third empty.
